title: Zeus, that it may be granted me
prose: Word reaches the king that **Sardis** has been taken and burnt by the **Athenians** and the **Ionians** together. **Darius** makes no account of the **Ionians** — he knows they will not escape — but he asks WHO THE ATHENIANS ARE, and has to be told. Then he asks for his bow. He takes it, sets an arrow on the string, and discharges it upwards into the sky. And he gives a standing order to one of his attendants: that when dinner is set before the king, he should say always, three times.

He brings a very large land-army and a very large naval force down to **Kilikia**, puts the army on the road, and boards a ship himself.

title: Thasos, and then the mountain
prose: **Thasos** is taken without a hand raised in its defence. **Macedonia** is made to serve. Then the fleet crosses from **Thasos**, works along the coast to **Acanthos**, and tries to get round **Mount Athos** — and a violent north wind falls on it. THREE HUNDRED SHIPS AND MORE THAN TWENTY THOUSAND MEN. **Herodotus** itemises how they died: taken by the sea monsters that fill that water, dashed on the rocks, drowned not knowing how to swim, dead of the cold. He reports it as *it is said*, and the monsters arrive in the same breath as the arithmetic.

title: And the army fares no better

title: The camp on the Aleïan plain
prose: They come down from the king to the **Aleïan plain** in **Kilikia** with a large and well-equipped land-army, and they encamp there — and while they are encamped THE WHOLE NAVAL ARMAMENT COMES UP TO THEM, gathered from the nations that had been ordered to furnish it.And with it the ships for carrying horses, WHICH DARIUS HAD ORDERED HIS TRIBUTARIES TO MAKE READY THE YEAR BEFORE. Purpose-built vessels, commissioned from subject cities twelve months ahead. This was never a raid.THE HORSES GO ABOARD FIRST and the army after them — that is the order **Herodotus** gives, and it is the only thing he says about the loading. Then **six hundred triremes** sail for **Ionia**.

title: A route chosen out of fear
